column1: # .github/image-sources.tsv — every place in this tree that produces a
# container image reference, and the rule it is held to.
# A tile from a signed catalog bundle is digest-pinned and checked by
# tileschema.ValidateImagePin. The platform sidecars used to carry tag defaults
# with environment overrides that passed through no validator at all — two
# rules for one kind of value, and until this file existed nothing said so.
# That gap is closed (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#534): every reference below is
# digest-pinned and every one of them, default or override, goes through
# ValidateImagePin before it is used. What this file still does is stop the gap
# reopening — a source that is neither `validated` nor `pending` fails the test
# in api/internal/catalog/parity_test.go, so a third rule cannot arrive without
#   validated  the reference passes tileschema.ValidateImagePin before use.
#   pending    it does not yet. `cite` names the issue that will make it.
# The test also fails on a row whose code no longer exists, because a row that
# outlives its source makes the validated count read higher than it is.

column7: The baked mesh server image. Digest-pinned from the embedded mesh-images.json, which the control-plane release publishes and the OS build reads. A tarball `docker load` records no RepoDigest, so the OS build also writes the image ID it resolved at pull time and the supervisor checks the loaded image against it.
The metrics store, pulled at observability enable. Digest-pinned; checked in NewDockerComposeSupervisor.

The collector, pulled per node at observability enable. Digest-pinned; checked in NewDockerComposeSupervisor and again in BuildCollectorCompose, which is the last place the reference is seen before it leaves the box.

The rule evaluator. Digest-pinned; checked in NewDockerComposeSupervisor.
